title: B-45 pilot: the number two at the start of a sentence and in hero-son, the word equals, the five new hint clips, and the B-42 welcome seam (a made-up name, then a greeting, a topic and the closing line)
note: Written by the voice-and-sound-director on 2026-11-02. Real lines of pack 0.11.0 said the way the full voicing will send them (explicit settings per kind: correct 0.5, question 0.6, hint 2 0.65, hint 3 0.7; similarity 0.8; eleven_v4_turbo; mp3_44100_64). Line clips take the voice_text of the master table and the respelling of content/voices.json. Nothing here changes a screen text. Added 2026-11-02 (B-42 seam check, docs/milestones/B42.md section 6): clips 51 to 54 per narrator. The name clip says only a made-up name that is not one of the children's; it is NOT the real name clip (that is a separate later step through the gateway, made at a parent's tap, never by Claude). The three lines after it are the exact welcome lines of the run.

clips.tests: The number two as the FIRST word of a sentence: "shTA-yim. kach sof-RIM." Stress on TA, a clean sh-t start, no gap, no extra syllable. (D was not heard at the start of a sentence, nor in hero-son.)
Two at the start of a question, and again after "ve-OD": "shTA-yim ve-OD shTA-yim, mul..." Both twos stressed on TA; the question at the end rises.
Two in the middle, with the word "equals" as the pack sends it today (plain letters): "sha-VE" or "SHA-ve"? Compare with the next clip.

clips.text: חָמֵשׁ. שָׁלוֹשׁ ועוד שתַּיִם שָׁוֶה חָמֵשׁ.
clips.tests: The same line with שָׁוֶה pointed: "sha-VE". If it is clearly better than the previous clip, the pack needs a pronunciation entry for שווה (120 lines).
Two inside a counted list at hint-3 steadiness: "shTA-yim, sha-LOSH, ar-BA, cha-MESH"; calm, even, nothing rushed.
New hint 2 (QA-B36-6). "The fingers show how many to give": soft and clear, nothing counted aloud.
New hint 2 (QA-B36-6). "Here is the number written right. We look at it well." Two short sentences; a small beat between.
New hint 2 (QA-B36-6). "Every pair in a ring, and we count pair after pair": the rhythm of pairs, calm.
New hint 2 (QA-B36-6). "Next to every coin it says how much it is worth": "sha-VE" in the plain text; which way does the voice read it?

The made-up name alone, as the call that opens a welcome: "da-NI," a short rise, a small pause, a quiet start. Same voice and settings as the greeting that follows. Made-up name only; a name of one of the children must never be used here.

Play it right after clip 51 with a gap of about 400 ms (play both, then try 300 and 500). Does "da-NI ... sha-LOM, EI-ze kef lir-OT et-KHEM" sound like one voice saying one sentence? Check: no click at the start, no long lead-in silence, same loudness as 51, "shalom" not louder or higher than the name.
The topic after the greeting: "ha-YOM nir-E ka-MA yesh be-ma-BAT e-KHAD." A light preview, level, no rise, not a promise. Same pace and loudness as the greeting before it.

The closing line: "bo-U nif-TAKH et ha-bak-BUK." Warm and short, a soft end, an invitation and not a command. Then listen to 51, 52, 53, 54 in a row (the whole welcome, about 8 s): too long? too even? pleasant for a 3 year old?
